evidence: p.5: 'Every quantitative value here carries an explicit evidence label — a dated measurement, a figure derived from cited inputs, an illustrative assumption, or a stated hypothesis; the three label axes behind those labels are defined in the Preface'; Preface p.16: 'The four terms above are not four parallel registers. issue: The copyright page summarizes the evidence system as one flat four-way choice of label kinds, but the Preface's operative system assigns each claim a two-axis pair (provenance + epistemic) with an optional third axis. The four listed kinds span the axes unevenly (no pure Axis-1 provenance item appears; 'an illustrative assumption' merges Axes 1 and 2), so the summary reintroduces the 'four parallel registers' reading the Preface explicitly rules out.
fix_instruction: Rewrite the sentence to name the three axes (where the number came from / what was done to it / measurement status) instead of enumerating four label kinds, or mirror the Preface panel's term-to-axis mapping verbatim.

issue: Evidence-tag drift against the book's own rules: (a) §5.7's [HYPOTHESIS] claims carry only the epistemic axis, with no paired provenance tag; (b) the Ch. 7/Ch. 8 caveat boxes close qualitative mechanism statements with a bare [DERIVED] even though nothing was 'computed by arithmetic from stated inputs' (DERIVED's definition); (c) §5.1.1–5.1.2 tag non-arithmetic methodology statements [1P][DERIVED]. The Preface requires a full Axis-1+Axis-2 pair for claims and reserves DERIVED for arithmetic.
fix_instruction: Pair each claim tag with an Axis-1 provenance (e.g. [canonical scenario][DERIVED] where the statement derives from canonical inputs), delete [DERIVED] from non-quantitative sentences, and re-tag the §5.1/§5.7 methodological and hypothesis statements with the correct axis pair (or no tag). Recurrence-sweep §7.3.2, §8.1.1–8.3.1 for the same bare-tag pattern.

chapter: Ch. 7 Memory Is the First Constraint

issue: The §7.1 error illustration names the wrong quantity pair: '165 GB fits in 160 GB' is self-falsifying (165 > 160), whereas the conflation error the book itself documents in §7.4 point 3 is concluding the 2×H100 host suffices from the 140 GB weight footprint alone (ignoring the ~24.1 GB KV). fix_instruction: Change the p.145 string to 'a "140 GB fits in 160 GB" error' (or 'the weights fit, so the host fits') so the illustration matches §7.4's own account of the common mistake.
